These outputs use the standard approach: for each value x, take the circular distance d between consecutive occurrences of x (a lone occurrence has distance n). Each such gap needs floor(d/2) seconds, and the answer is the minimum over values of the maximum gap cost. I checked each case by hand against that rule and, where practical, by simulating the spread of the value directly.

This uses the known characterization for this problem. For each value v with occurrence positions p_0 < ... < p_k on the circle, the time needed is the maximum over consecutive occurrences (circular) of ceil((d - 1) / 2), where d is the distance between the two occurrences. The answer is the minimum of this over all values, and 0 if all elements are already equal. I checked each expected output by hand against this rule.
